# CoSpace

> CoSpace is open-source software (MIT) that turns a Mac or Linux server into shared Linux dev spaces for people and AI coding agents. Guests join over plain `ssh`, with no account and no API key. Claude Code, Codex and Grok work inside each space on AI quota that the host provides through a credential gateway. Host credentials never enter a space.

CoSpace is for hosts who want to give people they trust a ready-to-run coding-agent environment on their own machine, with no signup and no cloud bill. It is also for people who want to work with a teammate's coding agent: one shared home directory holds the same files, the same Claude Code sessions and the same memory.

Key facts:

- Host: Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 26+ (each space is an Apple container Linux VM), or a Linux x86_64/arm64 server with Docker and systemd.
- Guests: macOS, Linux, Windows. They connect with standard ssh or Cursor Remote SSH.
- Host install: `curl -fsSL https://cospace.jingxuan.uk/host.sh | sh`
- Guest install: `curl -fsSL https://cospace.jingxuan.uk/install.sh | sh` (command `cospace`, alias `co`); Homebrew: `brew install jingxuankang/tap/cospace`
- The host controls each space: dollar budget cap, concurrency cap, per-provider switches, Internet access switch, instant revocation.
- Connectivity is peer-to-peer (embedded Tailscale library with DERP fallback). The vendor runs no server.
- Web console and guest CLI are in English and Simplified Chinese.
- Written in Go; single static binaries. Latest version: see GitHub Releases.
- Contact: hello@cospace.jingxuan.uk
